ratings_why.fun: Mid and late game are a joy: Bora and Vane openers at T3-4, then a crowned favourite under Lady High Pressure; the first three turns are thin.
ratings_why.distinct: Extra attacks are familiar, but Defer (courtiers handing their swing to the biggest unit) and a fight count the shop reads back are fresh.

verdict_why: The v1 rule holes are closed and nothing is a runaway with no counterplay; more passes would change it, not improve it.

points.text: Turns 1-3 lean on Gust Page alone for tempo; a second Tier 1 or Tier 2 body that wins early fights would smooth the climb before the Gale readers pay.
Gale Warnings stack on one unit permanently, so The Sí Gaoithe quietly builds a unit with many opening Gusts over a game; worth a look at turn 12 rather than per fight.
Mackerel Sky at Gale 10 is the tribe's main permanent board growth; with Master of the Wild Hunt doubling the Gale, the 10 step is easy, so it may be the one T4 you always take.
Bowing Zephyr is a nice early Defer teacher; letting it also count its Defer toward the Gale would give early Gale readers something to read.

standouts.why: Lady High Pressure turns the whole board into one favourite's queue: a real capstone that changes how you seat and buy.
Countess Bora gives a clean, readable T4 power spike: your whole front row swings before the enemy moves.
The Thunderhead lights its own fuse at Gale 6 and grows with every Gust after; late and loud, as the seed says.

weakest.why: Pine-Cone Augur is a slow seed that grows only after Gusty fights, which early you rarely have.
Red Sky at Night is a plain conditional gold unit with little tie to how you fight.
Cirrus Steward is a generic biggest-unit buffer; it works but adds no decision.

flags.note: Old Föhn with Lady High Pressure and The Swift Couriers makes a favourite that takes almost no return damage from its many Gusts; Bog folk and focused enemy attacks are the counter.
Golden Master of the Wild Hunt with golden Thunderhead gives about +12 Attack per Gust inside a fight; a high roll, but test it.
The Sí Gaoithe feeds its own condition and its Warnings are permanent, so opening Gusts accumulate across a game.
